findings.location: inner_product_design.tex Prop ip-konishi (l.320-336), Prop ip-twenty (l.338-349), Thm ip-logic (ii),(iv), Rem ip-tested, Thm ip-laws (d); engine_plan_ip.json IP5 (l.215, l.219) and prerequisites; engine_plan.json E3 and open_items
findings.claim: The real parts of the radial lines of T1 and T2 are not decisive as planned. q, s, q', s' come from arity-one computations along xi in S_+ (x) W and eta in S_+ (x) W^* whose arity-one finite counterterms carry a free multiple of S^(1)(xi), S^(1)(eta); on the pair (xi, xi^dagger) this multiple is the restriction of G_B and equally of exact inner directions (R_xi, Delta), all acting as q -> q - x, s -> s + x. Its real part is fixed only by reflection compatibility, which relates S_+ (x) W to its Theta_n image in S_- (x) W^*; no IP stage or prerequisite computes a component along S_- (x) W^*, and engine_plan.json expects Re a to be fixed BY the Q^dagger = S test. One radial line is therefore spent on Re a; the independent real content of T1 + T2 is the G_B-invariant difference of the two radial residuals (and T3, which is invariant). The IP5 covariance run 'outer direction a G_B with imaginary a ... the real part must break T1, T2' presupposes a baseline Re a = 0 that nothing in the plan establishes.
findings.evidence: engine_plan.json E3: 'state the solution family; it contains a S^(1)(xi) = a G_B^(1)(xi)'; odd_components_design.tex rem:o-alpha: the same term 'is the restriction to xi of G_B, and also of the exact cocycle d/dt (e^{t ad R_xi})^* S_psl'; rem:o-GBdagger and engine_plan.json open_items: 'Re a expected to be fixed by the Q^dagger = S test of R5 (c)'. ip_audit2_checks.json A2: with r = s_a - s_b (Thm ip-P (ii), C9) the inner direction gives (-t,+t) and the outer B gives (b,-b) on Q (3,1), S (1,3): same pattern; they differ only on S_- (x) W^* (inner -t, outer -b) and on P, K; reflection r(2,3) = r(3,1) with MC gives Re r_xi = r_P/2. A1: a real G_B coefficient a shifts the T2 radial residual by 2a; T1 identically. inner_product_checks.py C6 tests G_B only with imaginary a. engine_plan_ip.json prerequisites: E0, E1, E4, E5, E8, E10, E11, Part D (E12, the only item with S_- (x) W^* generators, appears only in the range 'E0-E12' of binding_inputs).
findings.fix: Add T2n/T1n: the reflection identity of Thm ip-logic (ii), <-Lambda^(1)(xi) a, b>_n = <a, -Lambda^(1)(xi^{dagger_n}) b>_n with xi^{dagger_n} = rho(n) conj(xi) in S_- (x) W^*, on (K, O_xi) and on the 20' pair, with Q_1 along one generator of S_- (x) W^* (extension of E5/E4, using the E12 machinery) and the reflection Gram from the IP1/IP2 two-point functions; or build F^(1) as the Theta_n average over S_+ (x) W + S_- (x) W^* in E3. Then the radial lines of T1 and T2 are both tests; otherwise state in Prop ip-konishi, ip-twenty and Rem ip-tested that the T2 radial line fixes Re a and only T1 - T2 and T3 test. CH08: cor:c8-gram: 'the conjugation fixes the real part of the outer direction' does not say which data fix it; proposed fix: replace by 'reflection compatibility (Theorem \ref{thm:c8-fields}) fixes the real part of the outer direction: the arity-one finite counterterm along $S_-\otimes W^*$ must be the $\Theta_n$-image of the one along $S_+\otimes W$'.

findings.location: engine_plan_ip.json IP0 (G0 by Thm ip-origin), IP5 (T1-T3, before any frame conversion), IP6 (l.234 'recompute G1 (multiplied by 1 + 2 c unit w)'); inner_product_design.tex Lemma ip-W (hypothesis P_1 = M_1 = R_1 = 0), Thm ip-origin, Thm ip-P (iii) (l.279), inputs of Prop ip-konishi ('q [odd, E5], s [odd, E8]')
findings.claim: Frame bookkeeping is inconsistent. By Lemma ip-W / Thm ip-origin the radial Gram equals the two-point coefficient at |y| = ell only in the frame P_1 = 0. The two-point function is not changed by the inner field redefinition phi ~ S^(1)(Delta) ((s phi)^(0) = 0; at separated points <{phi,O_1},O_2> + <O_1,{phi,O_2}> = 0, the tree dilatation Ward identity), so in the engines' frame (translation-invariant arity-one counterterm, P_1 = -(1/3+f) unit {S^(1)(P_b),-} on the scalar bilinears) the radial Gram is (1 - 2 c unit w) times the two-point coefficient. IP5 evaluates T1-T3 with E-plan generator data against the IP0-IP3 two-point Grams before IP6 converts frames: the T2 radial residual is 4 c_K - 5 c_zeta (-c for a universal c, i.e. +1/3 for c = -1/3), T1's 4 c_20' - 5 c_20, which is the pattern of a real G_B coefficient, so with IPA2-1 the error is absorbed silently. IP6 then multiplies the two-point G1 by (1 + 2 c unit w): that is the rule of route (b) (finite part psi' = c w, which does change the two-point function, tp prop:t-laws (F3)) applied to a Gram that already is the P_1 = 0 Gram of route (a); in the sl(2) model the K line then fails by -2c unit K_0. Thm ip-P (iii) presents routes (a) and (b) as interchangeable although they give the same generator matrices and two-point functions differing by 1 + 2 c unit w. The per-family frame data are known only for scalar bilinears (and letters); no task computes them for O_zeta, the 20, Fbar_w, B_w.
findings.evidence: ip_audit2_checks.json A1: frame-Z data satisfying T2 exactly, transported by U = diag(1 + 2 c_K u, 1 + (5/2) c_zeta u): exact with the frame-E Gram; with the two-point constants the residual is '4*c_K - 5*c_zeta', '-c' (universal), '1/3' (c = -1/3), absorbed by the real G_B coefficient '-2*c_K + 5*c_zeta/2'; 'two_point_unchanged_by_inner_redefinition': true. A3: K line exact with the two-point Gram (P_1 = 0); after IP6's rescaling residual -2c K_0 (entry (0,1) = -4cw). compare_delta.json: translation component -(1/3 + f_P) D_P O on scalar bilinears, 'B reports no such graphs for letters', trace bilinear output sectors '(A_V,A_V) and (c,A*_V) not computed'; delta_theory.tex prop:d-P (ii): 'c = -1/3 units, and c = 0 for the letters'. engine_plan_ip.json IP5 mentions frames only for T4 ('frame of P_1 from E11'); E11 covers 'letters and bilinears'.
findings.fix: In engine_plan_ip.json: compute, before IP5, the composite translation and dilatation remainders on every test family (K, 20', O_zeta, the 20, Fbar_w, B_w), checking that on each family (also the mixed-length weight-3 family) they are a multiple of the classical component; convert the E-plan matrices family by family, X -> U^{-1} X U with U = 1 + c_F unit w, and keep G0, G1 = two-point coefficients; delete 'recompute G1 (multiplied by 1 + 2 c unit w)' (equivalently work in the engines' frame with Gram_E = (1 - 2 c_F unit w) x two-point coefficient). In the design: Thm ip-P (iii) should keep only the field-redefinition route (a) for the identification of Thm ip-origin, or state that route (b) changes the two-point function by 1 + 2 c unit w and needs psi' on smeared operators (where c times the Weyl weight of the density does not commute with integration by parts); Prop ip-konishi, ip-twenty, ip-weight3 should state that q, s, q', s', U, V are taken in the frame P_1 = 0 of the respective families.

findings.location: engine_plan_ip.json IP1 'method' (l.119), IP2 'method': 'as IP1' (l.153), IP3, constraints.independence (l.19), comparison_protocol.independence (l.266); inner_product_design.tex section 'Engine plan' (l.426)
findings.claim: The engines are independent in code and outputs, not in method: IP1-IP3 prescribe one route for both (engine A's Beta/Dirichlet eps-expansion d4_integrals.py, restricted by its docstring to one-loop cycles with n <= 3 edges, inside the decomposition of tp thm:t-scalar: numerator identity, Lemma t-reduce, position-space masters J and R, the localisation constants of Lemma t-local, the Fourier lemma t-ft and the claim that the finite five-line graph is a pure contact term) and the same explicit census. Agreement of A and B would then not test the shared decomposition or census. The only planned second evaluation of the masters is finite-eps quadrature, which confirms the eps -> 0 constants only to O(eps log eps), not 'at a second precision'.
findings.evidence: engine_plan_ip.json l.119: '(engine A method d4_integrals.py); ... numeric confirmation of each master at eps = 1e-4, 1e-5 by direct quadrature (mpmath, 30 digits)'; l.153: 'as IP1'; step2/engine_a/d4_integrals.py docstring 'one-loop cycles ... (n <= 3: sympy, exact)'; step2/engine_b/method_notes.json: engine B's Part C/D route differs (closed-form masters J3, J2 in masters.py; finite-eps whole-graph numerics without Taylor expansion, 4.675873561680783 at eps = 1e-6 against 11/4 + 19/4 log(3/2)); step2/theory/two_point_example_run.txt: J_numeric/J_pred = 0.999912 at eps = 1e-4; no cross-imports between the two engines (grep).
findings.fix: Give engine B its own route for IP1-IP3: momentum-space Schwinger/Gaussian evaluation of each whole two-loop graph (including the five-line graph with its numerator) with its masters.py and the Fourier lemma, or position-space evaluation at several eps with exact eps-extrapolation; let each engine generate the census from its own vertex tables (as E1 does) and re-derive Lemma t-reduce, t-local, t-ft and the five-line contact claim instead of importing them; describe the finite-eps confirmation as O(eps log eps)-accurate and keep 'integer relations ... confirmed at a second precision' for eps-independent integrals only.

findings.location: inner_product_design.tex Thm ip-P (v) (l.285), Status (l.433); engine_plan_ip.json IP6 (l.233)
findings.claim: Thm ip-P (v) reads the engines' -1/3 as the coefficient z of the full S^(1)(Delta) and says the two-leg equation leaves 'z' free. The engine input is f_S, the coefficient of the A|_{W_R^perp}-sector part S_M|_perp, and at two legs S_M|_perp, S_M|_lambda, S_M|_V + S_M|_c and X are free separately. The scalar-bilinear data predict only f_S = -1/3; r_Delta = 0 on the fermionic test families involves the S_M|_lambda coefficient and composite remainders that are not computed. The cited source (delta_theory prop:d-z) fixes z by the arity-two equation along (K_b, P_b') with the arity-one counterterms along K_b, P_b', not along (Delta, P_b), where {S^(1)(P_b), S^(1)(Delta)} ~ S^(1)(P_b) enters together with the translation coefficient f_P.
findings.evidence: compare_delta.json comparisons_part1 [18]: 'free Q-closed directions S_M|_perp, S_M|_lambda, S_M|_V+S_M|_c, X'; part2: 'f_S = coefficient of S_M|_P in F(Delta)', 'F(Delta)|_perp contains -(1/3) S_M|_perp'; delta_theory.tex prop:d-z and eq:d-Fsol (z S^(1)(Delta) + G_Delta, G_Delta closed 'other than S^(1)(Delta)').
findings.fix: Restate (v) and the IP6 gate: 'r_Delta = 0 on the scalar bilinears requires f_S = -1/3 for the coefficient of S_M|_perp; on O_zeta, the 20 and Fbar_w it fixes the coefficient of S_M|_lambda; whether these are one coefficient z of S^(1)(Delta) is decided by the cubic arity-one equation and the (K_b, P_b') arity-two equation [delta_theory, prop:d-z]'; add the Delta-composite remainders of these families to IP6.

findings.location: inner_product_design.tex test-set table (l.390-404), Cor ip-D, Prop ip-Kline; engine_plan_ip.json IP3 outputs, IP5 covariance runs
findings.claim: The test set is not minimal. T5 (D_1 = D_1^adj) holds identically on the weight-2 and weight-5/2 test families (D_1 a real multiple of the identity by Schur) and on the weight-3 family it is equivalent to T3 (iii); the MC lines of T1, T2 are the operator-level arity-two identity that E9 already checks; the descendant part of T4 is the kinematic identity C4 and its K line is the MC identity at (K_b, P_b'); IP3's output m_F enters no relation of T0-T5 at the stated order; the IP5 covariance runs apply the transformation laws proved in C2, C6 to computed numbers and cannot fail unless graphs are recomputed. The decisive Q^dagger = S content is T3 (i)-(iii) and, after IPA2-1 and IPA2-2, the radial lines of T1 and T2.
findings.evidence: ip_audit2_checks.json A5: three complex trials; c_K from T3 (iii) makes Gram_tree D_1 exactly Hermitian, c_K + 1 does not (leading term of order unit^2 nonzero), and the Fbar-Fbar entry of D_1 vanishes at relative order unit; Example ip-scalars: 'D_1 is diagonal and real'; engine_plan.json E9; inner_product_checks.py C2, C4, C6.
findings.fix: Mark T5 on the weight-3 family as identical to T3 (iii) and move T5 to a family on which D_1 mixes and is computed independently of the supercharge data (dimension-4 singlets, or the 20' of [BERS]); label the MC lines and T4 as master-equation gates; drop m_F from IP3 or state its use; recompute at least one covariance run with a nonzero finite part inserted in the graphs.

findings.location: inner_product_design.tex Prop ip-orders (l.175, proof l.179); two_point_design.tex prop:t-census-w3; engine_plan_ip.json IP3 'order sqrt(unit)' (l.177)
findings.claim: The stated reason for the vanishing of the order-one-half entries between B_w and Fbar_w, F_n ('no graph with an even number of half-edges at this order: 3+2+3+3 and 3+2+4 are odd') is wrong: the order-one-half class is the tree with one cubic vertex, 3+2+3 = 8 half-edges, at relative order unit; the counts 3+2+3+3 and 3+2+4 belong to graphs that exist at no order. The entry vanishes by field content: the cubic vertex would need legs (A|_perp, A|_perp, lambda) or (A|_perp, A|_perp, lambdabar), which the action has not (tp prop:t-orderg (b)). IP3 'records as zero' without checking this class.
findings.evidence: ip_audit2_checks.json A4: classes for (B_w,F_n) and (Bbar,Fbar_w): one cubic vertex 8 half-edges, E = 4, b1 = 2, relative order unit^1, exists; one quartic 9 and two cubic 11 (do not exist); cubic+quartic and three cubic: b1 = 3, unit^2; matching cubic vertices for the needed legs: none.
findings.fix: Replace the parity sentence by the field-content argument of tp prop:t-orderg and add an IP3 gate: the one-cubic-vertex trees between B_w and Fbar_w, F_n vanish identically; keep b1 = 3 for the first nonvanishing classes.

[8] and assert the orthogonality from the U_B(1) bonus symmetry [21] (text after (11)); the point splitting (17) is used for the K_1 correlators only.
